subject: general
question: In 2019, with which international financial institution did India sign an agreement to operationalize two lines for the Mumbai Metro Rail System?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Asian Development Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is a regional development bank established on 19 December 1966, which is headquartered in Manila, Philippines.
 
• The ADB was founded to promote social and economic development in Asia.
 
• India signed an agreement with the ADB in 2019 to operationalize two lines for the Mumbai Metro Rail System.
 
• The agreement aimed to improve the efficiency of urban transport and ease traffic congestion in Mumbai, facilitating better connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Development Bank (ADB)**

 
 
• The ADB was established to foster economic growth and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
• It provides loans, technical assistance, grants, and equity investments to promote social and economic development.
 
• The bank has 68 members, 49 of which are from the Asia-Pacific region.
 
• ADB's operations are primarily directed at developing member countries, particularly those with low income, to reduce poverty and improve the quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Mumbai Metro Rail System**
 
 
• Mumbai Metro is a rapid transit system serving the city of Mumbai, Maharashtra.
 
• The system is designed to reduce traffic congestion in the city and supplement the overcrowded Mumbai Suburban Railway network.
 
• It is being implemented in multiple phases, with the first line inaugurated in June 2014.
 
• The project aims to improve public transportation, reduce travel time, and provide a modern, efficient, and sustainable means of transport for the residents of Mumbai.
